author: The Infographics Show
description:
Your credit score doesn’t matter as much as you think. Banks, AI lenders, Klarna, Affirm, Buy Now Pay Later apps, and the entire consumer debt system are quietly tracking a new kind of invisible debt, and it’s already changing who gets approved for mortgages.

Buy Now Pay Later was sold as harmless convenience. Split the payment, no interest, no stress.
But behind the scenes, retailers are quietly raising prices to offset massive BNPL transaction fees, meaning everyone pays more at checkout, even people who never use Klarna or Affirm.

At the same time, millions of Americans are stacking invisible debt across multiple BNPL apps while underwriters and AI systems increasingly flag this behavior as a financial risk.
What once stayed hidden is now starting to affect mortgage approvals, debt-to-income ratios, and credit decisions.

The entire system runs on one dangerous idea - make spending feel painless now, and deal with the consequences later.
